items.title: Selling an Android Phone: Privacy, Account Removal and Reset Checklist
items.dek: Prepare an Android phone for resale by checking backups, Google account removal, passkeys, eSIM and the factory reset before handover.
items.author: GAMIC News Editorial Desk
items.imageAlt: Illustration of mobile account removal and Android device transfer
body: Selling an Android phone is not simply a matter of deleting a few pictures. The device may contain signed-in accounts, payment apps, stored authentication material, downloaded files, location history, eSIM information and connections to smart-home devices. A factory reset can help remove personal data, but the safe order of operations matters. You want to keep access to your own accounts while handing the next owner a phone that can be activated normally.

This checklist is written for an ordinary personal phone, not a managed company device or a phone whose ownership is disputed. Android versions, manufacturers and carrier arrangements differ, so the exact names of settings may change. Google's official Android reset and account-management guidance provides the foundation. Check the instructions for your specific model before taking irreversible steps, and do not assume that removing a phone from one app clears every other service.

The most important principle is to verify every transfer before wiping the source device. A cloud backup that has not finished is not a backup you can rely on, and a replacement phone that has not accepted your authentication credentials may leave you locked out. Complete the checks before meeting the buyer rather than rushing through settings at the point of sale.
takeaways: Confirm backups and new-device account access before wiping.
Remove legitimate account links and transfer eSIM correctly.
Test the clean setup screen without signing back into the sold phone.

sections.heading: Confirm the phone is yours to transfer
paragraphs: Before listing the device, check whether it belongs to an employer, school, lease program or financing arrangement. A managed phone may be subject to enrollment restrictions that a factory reset does not remove. Carrier locks and unpaid obligations can also affect a buyer. Verify the specific model, storage capacity and condition without publishing personally identifying serial numbers in the advertisement. Honest details reduce disputes and protect both parties.

If you bought the phone second-hand, check that your ownership is legitimate and that previous accounts have been removed. Do not offer a device that still shows someone else's activation or management requirement. A factory reset should not be used to bypass anti-theft protection. Where an account or management policy blocks a transfer, contact the rightful administrator or seller through the official channel before attempting another wipe.

sections.heading: Inventory anything stored only on the device
paragraphs: Open your gallery, file manager, messaging apps, notes and voice recorder. Look for local photos, downloaded documents, contact files, authenticator exports and recordings that never synchronized. Some applications keep data in private storage that a general cloud photo backup does not include. List any items you cannot replace. If an app advertises its own backup or transfer feature, read what it covers before trusting a generic system backup to preserve its contents.

Pay particular attention to messaging histories and two-factor authentication tools. A replacement phone may restore a messaging app without restoring every old attachment or conversation. An authenticator may require a dedicated account transfer or fresh enrollment. Test those processes while the old device is still functional. Avoid taking unencrypted screenshots of recovery codes or storing them in a casually shared photo folder.

sections.heading: Back up the important data and verify recovery
paragraphs: Use the appropriate cloud or local backup process for your device and applications. Confirm the backup's completion date and whether the included data matches what you expect. A progress indicator alone does not guarantee that every application will restore the way you imagine. Verify some photos at original quality, check contacts from another signed-in device and ensure essential documents are accessible outside the phone.

Where possible, sign in to the replacement phone before resetting the old one. Test access to key accounts, banking tools and the messaging services you rely on. If a second device is not available, make a clear recovery plan using official service instructions and approved backup factors. A seller who keeps an old phone powered for one extra day to verify critical access is usually making a safer decision than someone who wipes it immediately after pressing Back up.

sections.heading: Move authenticator apps and passkeys safely
paragraphs: Sign-in credentials deserve separate treatment. Some passkeys synchronize through approved providers, while others can be device-bound. Authenticator apps may support cloud backup or explicit account transfer, but capabilities vary. Open each important service's security settings and check whether a new device or backup authenticator is registered. Do not rely on the existence of a phone-number recovery option if you are also changing your mobile number.

After enrolling a new factor, sign out and perform a genuine login test. If the account offers recovery codes, store them according to the provider's recommendations, not inside an unprotected gallery. An account may remain accessible on the old device even though your new login method is broken. That is exactly why the test must occur before a reset. Keep the recovery route secure but practical for a future device loss.

sections.heading: Understand what happens to SIM and eSIM
paragraphs: A physical SIM can generally be removed before handing over the device, while an eSIM is managed through the operating system and mobile carrier. The exact transfer or deletion steps depend on your carrier and model. If your replacement phone needs the same mobile number, complete the provider's activation or transfer process before erasing the old eSIM. Otherwise you may lose access to SMS verification and ordinary calls during the handover.

Removing an eSIM profile from a phone does not necessarily cancel the underlying subscription. Contact the provider when changing or ending a contract. Inspect the tray and remove memory cards as well as any physical SIM. Do not give the buyer an active mobile-service profile or a card containing personal photographs. When the phone is reset, confirm the setup flow no longer offers an unwanted subscriber identity.

sections.heading: Remove payment and wallet access
paragraphs: Phones often have digital wallets, transit cards, loyalty cards and payment applications. Review those services before the wipe, because some tokens or device registrations require separate management. A reset may remove locally stored app state, but a card can remain associated with an account elsewhere. Use the card issuer's or wallet provider's official controls when unlinking a device, especially if you are switching ecosystems.

Never share payment-app credentials with the buyer, even if the buyer says a refund or transfer requires them. If you have used the phone for work expenses or financial accounts, check sign-in history and enrolled devices from a separate trusted device after the sale. The goal is to prevent residual access and maintain your legitimate account continuity; it is not enough that the app icon disappears from the home screen.

sections.heading: Remove personal Google accounts before the reset
paragraphs: Google's reset guidance explains that device protection can be connected to the Google account and screen lock used on the phone. For an ordinary authorized resale, removing your account through device settings before the reset helps avoid handing the next owner a phone that still asks for your credentials. Exact menus and requirements vary. Check that you can sign into the account elsewhere before removing it from the old phone.

Do not tell a buyer your Google password to get past an activation screen. If you accidentally reset the device without clearing the relevant account relationship and the setup remains protected, follow Google's documented owner-recovery process. Anti-theft checks are designed to prevent unauthorized reuse. The safe approach is proper account removal and ownership verification rather than bypass instructions found on untrusted websites.

sections.heading: Disconnect watches, earbuds and other paired devices
paragraphs: Bluetooth accessories may retain relationships with the old phone. A smartwatch may have its own reset or migration requirements, including backups for health or activity data. Smart-home apps can expose device controls and household membership that should be reviewed separately. Unpair what you no longer intend the phone to control, then confirm that the replacement phone can use the accessories that matter.

Remember that some services maintain a cloud-side list of trusted devices. After migration, review authorized devices and remove the sold phone where appropriate. This is not the same operation as wiping local data, and doing only one may leave confusing entries or active sessions. Keep a short list of critical accounts and wearables to verify once the transfer is complete.

sections.heading: Perform the factory reset through official settings
paragraphs: Once backups, account migration, SIM management and device protection are handled, use the factory-reset process documented by Google or the device manufacturer. Do not use random flashing tools to perform a routine resale wipe. A normal authorized reset is designed to remove user data and restore initial setup behavior; the exact security properties depend on the device's encryption and implementation. Keep the phone charged or connected appropriately during the operation.

Read confirmation screens carefully because the reset deletes local data and cannot be undone from the phone itself. If a business or school profile exists, contact its administrator before proceeding. Avoid repeated experimental resets if the process fails; note the actual error and consult authorized support. When the device restarts, it should show an initial setup experience rather than your personalized account screens.

sections.heading: Verify the reset without signing back in
paragraphs: Inspect the first-boot setup flow after the reset. You should not see your personal home screen, gallery, contacts or unlocked accounts. Confirm that the phone is not prompting for an account that only you can supply as a normal next-owner activation step. Do not complete setup with your own Google account just to demonstrate the phone works; doing so can recreate the account relationship you intended to remove.

Check that the handset's buttons, charging connector, display and cameras function as expected using permissible setup or diagnostic methods that do not reintroduce personal data. If you are handing the buyer a charger, disclose compatibility and condition accurately. Keep evidence of the reset and transfer where helpful, while avoiding photos that expose full serial identifiers or private account details in public marketplace listings.

sections.heading: Review online account sessions after handover
paragraphs: After the sale, sign in from a trusted device to the security pages of important services and review the list of devices or sessions. Remove the sold phone when it is still recorded as authorized and no longer needed. Check primary email, cloud photos, password management and payment platforms first. This is an account-maintenance step, not a reason to send remote commands to a device you no longer own.

If a service sends an alert about a login from the old phone after handover, investigate it through the service's official account page. Change credentials and revoke sessions if the evidence justifies it. Keep ownership-transfer receipts and marketplace messages in case a dispute arises. Proper closure involves both local data removal and the associated service-side permissions that survive on remote servers.

sections.heading: Protect yourself during the sale
paragraphs: Meet buyers through safe marketplace practices. Avoid sharing activation codes, recovery links or account credentials to prove ownership. A buyer can inspect the phone's physical condition and setup screen without accessing your private accounts. Describe known battery and screen issues plainly; cosmetic photos should avoid displaying notification previews or personal names. If you are mailing the device, remove cards and accessories that are not included in the sale.

Keep a record of the agreed condition, payment and handover. If the buyer reports that activation is blocked, distinguish a legitimate account-removal oversight from a request to disclose your password. Resolve genuine transfer errors through official support or an appropriate return process. You should never need to compromise another account to make a used device sale go through.

items.title: How to Stop Chrome Website Notification Spam Without Losing Important Alerts
items.dek: Find which website is sending fake virus notices or unwanted Chrome notifications, block it precisely and keep your useful alerts.
items.author: GAMIC News Editorial Desk
items.imageAlt: Original illustration of a browser notification and privacy controls
body: A fake virus warning may look like a system alert even when it actually came from a website that was allowed to send Chrome notifications. That distinction matters. Installing a random cleaner, reinstalling the browser or changing every pop-up setting is often unnecessary if the problem is a specific site's permission. The first task is to identify the sender and stop that permission, while preserving any useful reminders you intentionally receive.

Chrome separates website notifications, pop-up windows, redirects and browser extensions. Each has a different control. A notification can appear even when no tab for that website is open; a pop-up is generally a window or browser action initiated by a page. Some scams imitate security software or operating-system messages. This guide works from the least disruptive fix toward broader checks, rather than asking you to disable every useful browser feature.

The instructions refer to Chrome's site settings as documented by Google. Menu labels can vary with language, operating system and browser updates. Always use the browser's own settings interface, check the website domain before trusting an alert and avoid calling a telephone number displayed in a frightening notification. An unsolicited message is not evidence that your computer has been scanned or that its sender has access to your files.
takeaways: Identify the sender before changing unrelated settings.
Block or reset the specific site permission in Chrome's Notifications settings.
Distinguish push notifications, pop-ups and extensions during troubleshooting.

sections.heading: Identify whether the alert is a website notification
paragraphs: Notice where the warning appears. A Chrome website notification may appear in the operating system's notification area with a site name or origin attached, while a browser pop-up usually opens inside or above a browser window. Do not click on the notification's big action button merely to investigate its source. Look for a small domain label, browser icon or notification history entry. The sender's actual website address is more useful than a title claiming to be from security support.

If several alerts arrive, write down the domains before closing them. This helps distinguish one abusive publisher from unrelated legitimate apps. Be cautious with misspelled names that resemble established security companies. A notification with dramatic language, a countdown, a toll-free number or a demand for immediate payment should be treated as an unverified claim. If you are unsure, open the security product independently rather than using the alert's link.

sections.heading: Remove permission from the offending site
paragraphs: In desktop Chrome, open Settings, then Privacy and security, Site settings and Notifications. Review the list of websites currently allowed to send notifications. Locate the unfamiliar or disruptive domain and change its permission to Block or remove the permission, depending on the control offered in your version. Google documents these steps in its Chrome notification help article. You can often reach the same control by visiting a website, selecting the site-information icon near the address and modifying Notifications.

Remove only the permissions you recognize as unwanted at first. If an important calendar, collaboration tool or news service sends alerts you genuinely use, leave it enabled while you investigate the suspicious sender. If the site no longer appears in the list, check whether Chrome has automatically removed permissions from a site you have not visited recently. The absence of a site permission means the next alert may be coming from a different source.

sections.heading: Know the difference between Block and Remove
paragraphs: Blocking a site explicitly tells Chrome not to display notifications from that origin. Removing an exception resets its permission so a future visit may bring another request, depending on browser settings and Chrome's protections. For a clearly abusive sender, an explicit block may be easier to understand and preserve. The exact buttons vary by platform, so read the description rather than assuming a Delete or Reset action has the same meaning in every Chrome release.

There is no need to erase your entire browsing history just to revoke one site's push permission. Clearing cookies can sign you out of useful accounts without resolving alerts from another permitted origin. After changing the notification permission, close the unwanted alert and observe whether new alerts from that source stop. If they continue, verify that the setting was changed in the correct Chrome profile and that another browser has not been left open.

sections.heading: Reduce disruptive notification prompts in the future
paragraphs: Chrome supports notification defaults, including blocking requests or allowing quieter prompts. If you rarely want website push alerts, a broad default block can be appropriate. If you need alerts from work tools or a few trusted services, quieter prompts may be a better compromise. The objective is to prevent unfamiliar pages from taking your attention while preserving the specific sources you deliberately selected. The browser's notification settings describe what each option will change.

Before granting a new site's request, ask what benefit it actually offers. A restaurant menu, file download page or article does not normally require permission to send messages after you leave. Some sites make notification permission look like a prerequisite for playing media or proving you are human. Treat that pattern as a warning. Reject the request and use the site's core features only when they are genuinely available without granting unrelated permissions.

sections.heading: Check Chrome on Android separately
paragraphs: Chrome's Android notification controls overlap with system-level app notifications, and the available menus depend on Android version and manufacturer. A website may be blocked within Chrome even while Chrome itself remains allowed to display legitimate app notices. Start by inspecting the browser's site notification settings and identify the offending origin. If you turn off every notification for the Chrome app at the Android level, you may also silence notifications you actually wanted to keep.

When an alert appears on a phone, long-pressing it may show the app responsible or lead to notification controls. Use that clue to determine whether Chrome, another browser or an installed app sent the message. Avoid deleting an app based only on a claim made by the notification itself. Once you have identified the source, block the precise website permission or review the relevant application's notification settings as appropriate.

sections.heading: Do not confuse pop-ups with push notifications
paragraphs: Chrome normally blocks many intrusive pop-up windows, but that protection does not automatically cancel permissions previously granted for website push notifications. If advertising tabs or windows are opening while you browse, inspect Site settings, Pop-ups and redirects in addition to Notifications. Google's help documentation describes the controls separately. A successful change to the pop-up blocker should not be interpreted as proof that all notification permissions are safe or necessary.

Use a controlled observation: first close existing tabs, then wait to see whether a new notification appears without browsing. If it does, website push permissions or applications are more likely candidates. If an unwanted window appears only when you click a particular page, investigate that site's redirects and scripts. Avoid clicking through multiple prompts to reproduce suspicious behavior. Your aim is to narrow the source without increasing exposure to malicious pages.

sections.heading: Audit extensions without deleting everything
paragraphs: Extensions can alter browsing behavior, introduce new pages and display their own messages. Open Chrome's extension manager and review entries you do not recognize, especially those recently installed around the time unwanted alerts began. Examine permissions and the publisher information when available. If an extension appears suspicious, disable it and test whether the symptom changes. Removing every extension at once destroys the comparison and may interrupt password managers or accessibility tools.

Some legitimate extensions request broad access because of their features, but that does not justify permission you cannot explain. Prefer tools from identifiable publishers with clear functionality. If an extension was installed outside your usual process or cannot be disabled, investigate browser management policies and installed software. A work or school device may be managed by an administrator; bypassing those settings can be inappropriate and ineffective.

sections.heading: Look for signs of actual device compromise
paragraphs: A deceptive website notification alone is not proof of malware. However, additional symptoms deserve investigation: an unknown app launching at startup, the homepage repeatedly changing, unauthorized account sign-ins or security controls being disabled. Use the operating system's built-in security tools and update mechanisms. For Windows, inspect installed applications and run an appropriate scan using software you opened independently. Do not download a scanner advertised by the very warning you are trying to remove.

If there are credible signs that an account was compromised, change its password from a trusted device and review active sessions and recovery information. Where supported, enable phishing-resistant sign-in such as a passkey. The response should fit the evidence. One noisy permission is a browser-settings problem; confirmed unauthorized access is an account-security problem. Treating them as identical can waste time and create more risk than it removes.

sections.heading: How to investigate multiple Chrome profiles
paragraphs: Desktop Chrome can maintain separate profiles for personal, work and family browsing. Each profile may have its own extension list and website permissions. If you block a domain in one profile but continue seeing its alerts, check which profile was active when permission was granted. An alert's sender and app association can help you identify the relevant profile. Avoid assuming that a notification setting applies globally to every Chrome profile on your computer.

The simplest way to test is to close all Chrome windows, reopen only the profile you think is responsible and inspect its site notification exceptions. Repeat with another profile only if the symptom persists or records point there. Keep notes on which profiles permit the suspicious domain. On shared computers, make changes only to accounts you manage or have permission to configure; another person's legitimate reminders should not be silently disabled.

sections.heading: What to do when an alert pretends to be antivirus software
paragraphs: Fake security alerts use urgency to get users to click links, enter payment information, install software or contact a supposed support technician. The sender may use a familiar logo or name, but a website push notification is not an authenticated message from that organization. Close it, inspect the domain in Chrome settings and open your actual security software through its installed application or official website if you want to check device status.

Do not share remote access, credit-card details or one-time account codes with someone reached through an unsolicited alert. If you already provided information, respond based on what was shared: contact the payment provider for card exposure, review device security after remote access and update compromised account credentials. The notification settings fix stops the messages, but it cannot reverse financial or account actions taken earlier. Preserve relevant records when reporting a scam.

sections.heading: A safe troubleshooting order that preserves useful alerts
paragraphs: Begin by identifying the app and domain that sent the alert. Next, revoke that one site's notification permission. Then review your default notification-request behavior so future websites cannot easily repeat the pattern. If the alert stops, there is little benefit to deeper changes. If it persists, inspect other browser profiles, extensions and installed applications. This order protects useful browser settings and produces a clear record of what changed at each stage.

After each change, wait for a reasonable observation period rather than immediately making several unrelated changes. A sender may publish notices intermittently, so one quiet minute is not definitive. Keep a brief list of the domains you blocked and why. If a required work application unexpectedly stops alerting, return to its known official domain and adjust that specific permission rather than reverting every security setting on the browser.

sections.heading: Common questions and misconceptions
paragraphs: Blocking website notifications is not the same as blocking cookies, disabling JavaScript or disconnecting from the internet. Those settings control different functions and can break useful websites. Similarly, seeing Chrome's name beside a notification does not mean Google endorsed its message. Chrome is simply one application capable of relaying notifications from websites after permission is granted. The site identity and permission history are the relevant clues when deciding what should be trusted.

Another frequent mistake is allowing a notification permission merely to dismiss a full-screen request. A trustworthy page should make its actual purpose clear. If a website claims you must press Allow to verify that you are not a robot, examine whether you are being manipulated into subscribing to push messages. Chrome's controls make these permissions reversible, but the easiest fix is not granting them to a source you do not trust in the first place.

items.title: Controller Input Lag on PC: Diagnose Bluetooth, USB and Game Delay
items.dek: A controlled checklist for separating wireless interference, cable and port faults, firmware, frame pacing, display latency and game-specific behavior.
items.author: GAMIC News Editorial Desk
items.imageAlt: Original editorial diagram comparing controller input over Bluetooth and USB with a frame timeline
items.imageCredit: Original topic-specific vector illustration created in-house by GAMIC News
items.imageRights: Copyright GAMIC News; original editorial artwork with no third-party logos or game assets
body: To diagnose controller input lag on a PC, first decide whether the delay is in the controller link, the game, frame delivery or the display. Reproduce one simple action in one game, then compare the same controller by a known data-capable USB cable and by its supported wireless connection. Keep frame rate, V-Sync, display mode and game settings unchanged during that comparison.

A delayed feeling is real to the player, but it does not identify the layer at fault. Bluetooth interference can cause missed or bunched inputs; an unstable frame rate can postpone when an input becomes visible; a television picture mode can add display processing; and a game can filter analog movement by design. Changing every setting at once may improve the symptom while destroying the diagnosis.

Use official firmware and Bluetooth guidance, avoid unofficial polling-rate modifications, and stop using a swollen battery, damaged cable or hot connector. This guide provides a repeatable comparison rather than a universal millisecond promise, because controllers, radios, games, displays and measurement methods differ.
takeaways: Compare wired and wireless modes with the same controller, game route and frame settings.
Distinguish delayed display response from dropped, repeated or bunched controller inputs.
Update controller firmware through the maker's official tool and fix Bluetooth through documented Windows steps.
Do not use unsigned drivers, polling hacks or random latency utilities as the first test.

sections.heading: Define the symptom before changing settings
paragraphs: Write down what the controller actually does. A consistent delay between a button press and an on-screen action differs from an input that is missed, repeated, held after release or delivered in a burst. Analog-stick drift, a large dead zone and slow camera acceleration can feel like latency but are different behaviors. Test a digital menu movement and a digital action as well as an analog movement so the report does not reduce every symptom to one word.

Note whether the problem begins immediately, only after several minutes, only at a distance, or only when another wireless device is active. Record the controller model, connection mode, Windows build, game build, display and any remapping software. If the controller behaves incorrectly in Windows menus or an official test surface outside the game, the game is less likely to be the only cause. Do not use an untrusted web tester that demands unusual permissions.

sections.heading: Build one repeatable input test
paragraphs: Choose a game menu or training area where one button produces an obvious response without network dependence. Stand in the same location and repeat a short sequence: press, release, move, stop. Keep resolution, frame cap, V-Sync, upscaling and display mode constant. Record a short high-frame-rate phone video only if you understand that it can compare two setups but does not provide laboratory latency by itself.

Run the sequence after a fresh controller connection, then again when the symptom normally appears. A competitive online match is a poor first test because server latency and simulation can change independently. If the issue exists only online, compare an offline mode before blaming Bluetooth. The purpose is to create the smallest route that another person can repeat, not to produce a single impressive millisecond number.

sections.heading: Compare a real USB data connection
paragraphs: Use a known data-capable cable, not a charge-only cable, and connect directly to the computer for the comparison. Confirm that Windows recognizes the controller over USB rather than continuing to use the wireless link. If practical, temporarily turn the controller's wireless connection off or remove the pairing only after noting how to restore it. Repeat the same game route without changing any graphics or display option.

If wired mode eliminates missed or bunched inputs, investigate the radio path. If the controller remains consistently delayed in both modes, the game, frame queue, remapping layer or display becomes more plausible. If USB disconnects when the cable moves, inspect the connector and try another official or standards-compliant data cable. Do not hold a damaged plug at an angle as a permanent fix; intermittent power or data can corrupt the comparison and damage the port.

sections.heading: Check frame time before blaming the controller
paragraphs: An input can be received promptly but appear late because the game produces frames slowly or unevenly. Display a trustworthy in-game frame-time graph if one is available. Reproduce the action during stable performance and during the reported delay. A 30 frames-per-second cap naturally provides fewer visual update opportunities than 120 frames per second, while a severe hitch can postpone the visible result much longer than the controller transport.

Do not disable every synchronization feature at once. Record the current frame cap, V-Sync and low-latency option, then change only one supported setting for a comparison. A setting that reduces latency may introduce tearing or unstable pacing, so it is a tradeoff rather than a universal correction. If input feels delayed exactly when frame time spikes, investigate the rendering or CPU workload alongside the controller instead of applying radio fixes alone.

sections.heading: Separate display processing from input transport
paragraphs: Televisions and some monitors can add image processing for motion smoothing, noise reduction or scaling. Use the display's documented game or low-latency mode for one comparison, and confirm the PC is connected to the intended input. Do not copy service-menu changes from another model. Keep the controller connection fixed while changing display mode; otherwise an improvement cannot be assigned to either layer.

A display problem normally delays the visible response to keyboard and controller input alike. Compare a wired keyboard action in the same local menu when appropriate. If both feel delayed, inspect the display and frame pipeline. If only one controller has missed or repeated inputs while another device is clean, the controller path deserves more attention. Photograph the original picture settings before changing them so color and accessibility adjustments can be restored.

sections.heading: Troubleshoot Bluetooth with official Windows steps
paragraphs: Microsoft's Bluetooth guidance begins with confirming that Bluetooth is enabled, checking the device state, running the relevant troubleshooter, restarting the radio and examining driver updates. Follow the current Windows instructions for the installed version. Remove and pair the controller again only after recording the existing pairing and verifying that you can complete the process. Pairing repeatedly without fixing a radio or driver problem adds noise rather than evidence.

Check whether the Bluetooth adapter is internal, attached by USB or integrated with Wi-Fi. An external adapter hidden behind a metal desktop can have a poor radio path. Use a supported extension or front port only if the adapter maker permits it, and keep the test arrangement stable. Do not download a generic Bluetooth driver from a driver-aggregation site. Use Windows Update, the computer maker or the adapter maker's official package for the exact hardware.

sections.heading: Reduce wireless interference methodically
paragraphs: For one test, move the controller closer with a clear line of sight and move high-traffic wireless devices away from the adapter. USB 3 devices and hubs, crowded 2.4 GHz networks and a desktop case can affect radio conditions, but proximity alone does not prove which source is responsible. Change one physical factor at a time and repeat the same input route. Record distance and adapter location so the result can be reproduced.

Do not permanently disable Wi-Fi, security devices or essential peripherals merely to improve a gamepad. If moving one USB device or adapter clearly restores stability, test the arrangement twice before settling on cable management or a supported extension. A proprietary controller receiver may behave differently from Bluetooth; treat it as a third connection mode and identify it accurately rather than calling every wireless path Bluetooth.

sections.heading: Update controller firmware through official tools
paragraphs: Controller firmware can address connectivity and compatibility, but the update must come from the manufacturer. Xbox Support documents updates through the Xbox Accessories app or supported console paths. Sony provides its official updater for supported controllers on Windows. Read the current compatibility and connection requirements, keep the cable stable and do not interrupt power during an update.

Record the firmware version before and after if the tool exposes it, then repeat the same route. Do not claim that an update fixed latency if graphics or display settings changed at the same time. Avoid firmware files and flashing utilities from forums. If the official updater cannot detect the controller, troubleshoot the cable, USB path and supported operating system before attempting more invasive steps.

sections.heading: Inspect Steam Input and remapping layers
paragraphs: Steam Input, game launchers, accessibility tools and controller-vendor software can translate or remap input. Translation is useful, but two active remapping layers can create conflicts, wrong button prompts or duplicated actions. Record which layers are enabled for the affected game. Test the title with its documented native controller support or one translation layer at a time, without deleting a carefully built accessibility profile.

A game-specific Steam Input setting can explain why one title behaves differently while Windows and other games are normal. Consult Valve's current controller support documentation and the game's own support notes. Do not install kernel-level remapping drivers or unsigned filters as a first response. If disabling an optional remapper fixes the symptom, re-enable it once to confirm, export its profile if possible and update or report that component.

sections.heading: Check battery, cable and power behavior
paragraphs: Low battery can reduce wireless reliability or trigger disconnects depending on the controller design. Charge with the supported method, confirm the indicator and repeat the test. A battery that is swollen, leaking or unusually hot requires immediate retirement and manufacturer guidance. Do not puncture, compress or continue charging a damaged pack. Replace disposable cells as a matched set according to the controller instructions.

For USB testing, watch for Windows connection sounds or an on-screen device reconnect. Try a second known-good data cable and a direct port before assuming the controller electronics have failed. Hubs and front-panel wiring add another link; they can be tested later. If the connector is loose on the controller itself, a cable swap may change the symptom without providing a durable repair.

sections.heading: Compare another game and another controller carefully
paragraphs: Test one other local game with known controller support while preserving the same connection mode. If only one title is affected, inspect its input settings, patches, dead-zone controls and known issues. If every title shows the same missed inputs, the controller, connection or system layer becomes more plausible. A browser test is not a perfect substitute because browser scheduling and page code add their own variables.

If available, compare another supported controller on the same USB port and wireless adapter. Then compare the original controller on another supported device. These crossed tests help separate device and host, but avoid moving immediately to a console or phone with different firmware and polling behavior and declaring the numbers equivalent. The useful result is categorical: symptom follows controller, follows PC, follows wireless mode or follows one game.

sections.heading: Avoid misleading latency fixes
paragraphs: Unofficial overclocked polling drivers, timer-resolution utilities, blanket USB power edits and registry packs can change system behavior and security without isolating the cause. A higher advertised polling rate does not guarantee a lower complete input-to-photon delay, and an unstable USB configuration can create drops. Keep supported drivers and create a restore point before any documented system-level change.

Likewise, do not present a single phone-camera calculation as universal hardware truth. Camera frame rate, display scanout, game loop position and button actuation all influence the observation. Use simple recordings to compare before and after under the same setup. For purchasing decisions, prefer measurements from laboratories that disclose equipment, sample size, firmware, connection mode, game and display rather than anonymous latency tables.

sections.heading: Build an actionable support report
paragraphs: A good report includes controller model, firmware, connection mode, Bluetooth adapter or receiver, Windows build, USB cable and port, game build, remapping software, frame cap, display mode, battery state and exact reproduction steps. State whether the issue is consistent delay, missing input, repetition or disconnection. Include which crossed tests were clean and which reproduced the fault.

Send a game-only issue to the developer with its configuration and input layer. Send cross-game wireless failures to the controller, adapter or PC maker with the wired comparison. Stop troubleshooting and seek repair for heat, battery damage, broken ports or repeated disconnections with known-good cables. The objective is not to eliminate every millisecond; it is to identify the failing layer safely and retain a configuration that can be reproduced.

items.title: Free PC Game Storage Space Without Losing Saves: A Safe Cleanup Guide
items.dek: A reversible way to reclaim Windows gaming storage by measuring what is large, protecting saves, using official uninstall and storage controls, and verifying every change.
items.author: Eli Morgan
items.imageAlt: Original editorial illustration of a PC storage meter with protected game saves
items.imageCredit: Original topic-specific editorial artwork generated in-house by GAMIC News
items.imageRights: Copyright GAMIC News; original deterministic artwork with no third-party logos or game assets
body: To free PC gaming space safely, measure usage before deleting anything, identify which launcher owns each game, and back up local saves under the developer's instructions. Use the launcher's uninstall or move controls and Windows Storage settings instead of deleting protected folders by hand. After each change, confirm the recovered capacity, verify remaining games and keep the backup until cloud synchronization and the intended save are both proven.

A full drive can block game updates, Windows servicing and temporary installation work, but random cleanup can remove irreplaceable saves, mods, screenshots or configuration. The large game folder is not always the only storage consumer, and the presence of cloud sync is not a promise that every local file is recoverable. A safe cleanup separates replaceable application data from personal progress and changes one category at a time.

This guide relies on Microsoft's current Storage and Storage Sense documentation plus platform-supported library management. It avoids registry cleaners, disk-optimizer promises and blanket deletion of caches or WindowsApps. Exact launcher menus and save locations change, so check the publisher's documentation for each game before moving or deleting anything.
takeaways: Measure the system and game drives before cleanup and record the starting free space.
Back up confirmed local save folders and mod profiles before uninstalling or moving a title.
Use launcher move or uninstall controls; do not delete WindowsApps or package folders manually.
Review Storage Sense and Cleanup recommendations item by item, especially Downloads and Recycle Bin.
Verify save progress, screenshots, mods and recovered capacity before deleting backups.

sections.heading: Measure the storage problem before deleting files
paragraphs: Open File Explorer and Windows Settings, System, Storage to record capacity and free space on the system drive and every game drive. Note which bar is red or close to full and whether the problem appeared during an install, update or normal play. Take a screenshot or write down the values. A measured baseline prevents claims that a cleanup worked when space changed because a temporary installer completed or Windows removed files independently.

Review Storage used on other drives so a large secondary library is not confused with a full system drive. Windows and launchers can require temporary room on C even when a game lives elsewhere. Check the size of the pending game or update, but do not treat its download size as the only requirement. Package extraction, patching and rollback can consume additional working space that varies by title and platform.

sections.heading: Inventory game libraries by launcher
paragraphs: List Steam, Xbox app, Epic Games, GOG, publisher launchers and standalone titles installed on the computer. Open each launcher's official storage or library view and record its large games. Avoid relying only on a third-party disk scanner, because a folder name may not explain ownership or whether the launcher expects it. A title split between base files, downloadable content and mod tools can occupy more than one location.

Mark games as actively played, temporarily inactive or safe to reinstall later. Also identify capture libraries, shader caches, workshop content, mod downloads and installer archives. These categories need different treatment. A 100 GB game obtained from a store is usually replaceable; a 2 MB local save, custom mod profile or unpublished screenshot may not be. Storage decisions should reflect recoverability, not just size.

sections.heading: Identify where each game keeps saves
paragraphs: Consult the game's developer or publisher documentation for save locations and cloud support. Saves may be stored in Documents, Saved Games, AppData, the launcher userdata hierarchy or inside a profile managed by the game. Do not assume the installation directory contains progress. Some titles separate campaign saves, settings, photos and mods, while others use a publisher account in addition to platform cloud sync.

Confirm whether the game supports Steam Cloud, Xbox cloud saves or another service and whether the last synchronization completed. Cloud support can cover only selected files and may propagate an older or unwanted version. Before cleanup, exit the game normally, wait for the launcher to finish synchronization and preserve the confirmed local files. Record the account and profile associated with them without storing passwords.

sections.heading: Create a verified save backup
paragraphs: Copy the complete documented save folder to a separate location, preserving names and subfolders. Label it with game, profile, device and date. If the game supports manual export, use that feature as an additional copy. Do not edit binary saves or combine files from different slots. An external drive provides separation from the internal disk, but it should be safely ejected and stored securely.

Verify that the backup exists, has plausible size and contains files dated around the last trusted session. If possible, create an archive and test that it opens without replacing the live save. Keep screenshots of the in-game progress and save-selection screen. A backup is only useful when you can identify which game and state it represents; an unlabeled folder copied months ago can create another conflict.

sections.heading: Protect mods, screenshots and controller profiles
paragraphs: Mods can live in the game directory, a manager staging folder, workshop content or user profile. Export the mod manager profile and load order where supported, then record versions. Do not assume cloud save services include mods. Custom maps, reshade presets, accessibility mappings and configuration files may require their own backup. Note which items can be downloaded again and which are personal creations.

Move screenshots and captured videos through their launcher or capture-app library when possible. Verify that the destination files open before removing originals. Large clips can free substantial space with less risk than changing application packages, but they may contain private voice or account information. Store them according to your privacy needs rather than uploading everything automatically to a cloud service.

sections.heading: Use Windows Cleanup recommendations carefully
paragraphs: Microsoft's Cleanup recommendations can identify temporary files, large or unused files, cloud-synced files and unused apps. Review each group rather than choosing all. Downloads can contain driver installers, purchased assets or save backups; Recycle Bin can contain files you expected to recover. Previous Windows installations can support rollback for a limited period, so understand that consequence before removal.

Record the selected categories and run one cleanup. Recheck free space afterward. Do not use a third-party registry cleaner to gain disk capacity; registry entries are not the large game assets filling the drive, and aggressive cleanup can damage application registration. If Windows reports a full Temp folder, follow the specific Microsoft support route instead of deleting every hidden folder with an administrator command.

sections.heading: Configure Storage Sense without surprising deletions
paragraphs: Storage Sense can remove temporary files and manage Recycle Bin or Downloads according to chosen settings. Microsoft's documentation notes that behavior depends on configuration and that the feature primarily works on the system drive. Open its settings before enabling it and choose a schedule that matches your needs. Pay special attention to Downloads and cloud-content options rather than accepting assumptions from an older tutorial.

Run Storage Sense manually once only after reviewing the summary. Keep game-save backups outside folders subject to automatic cleanup. If a cloud provider marks files online-only, confirm that important files are actually downloaded before travel or system recovery. Storage Sense is a maintenance tool, not a game-save manager, and it should not be expected to understand which mod or configuration file is irreplaceable.

sections.heading: Move supported game installations instead of copying folders
paragraphs: Many launchers provide a move, change drive or library management feature. Use that supported control because it updates the platform's records and can validate the destination. Ensure the target drive has enough space, uses a supported file system and remains connected throughout. Do not drag a protected package folder to another drive and hope the launcher discovers it automatically.

After moving one game, launch it, load a known save and close normally before moving another. Check desktop shortcuts and mod-manager paths. A move can free space while avoiding a full redownload, but it does not automatically relocate screenshots, workshop staging or publisher-launcher caches. Measure both drives again and retain the save backup until the new location works across a restart.

sections.heading: Uninstall inactive games through the owning platform
paragraphs: Choose a large inactive game with a verified backup and known redownload route. Uninstall through the launcher or Windows Installed apps where the publisher instructs. Read any prompt about user data. Do not assume every uninstaller preserves saves, and do not delete the folder manually before the platform completes. Record downloadable content and edition so the correct package can be restored later.

Once uninstall finishes, inspect free space and confirm that unrelated games still launch. Some residual folders may contain saves or mods; identify them before removal. A remaining folder is not automatically junk, while a removed game can leave a launcher cache elsewhere. If the recovered capacity is much smaller than expected, use Windows storage categories and the launcher's library report to locate the difference rather than repeating uninstall.

sections.heading: Treat caches as replaceable only when documented
paragraphs: Shader, download and launcher caches can grow, but deleting them may trigger long recompilation, repeat downloads or new stutter. Clear a cache only through the application's supported control or current documentation. Confirm that it does not include saves, offline licenses or mod packages. The word cache is descriptive, not a guarantee that every folder with cache in its name is safe to erase.

Clean one cache at a time and measure its size first. Afterward, launch the relevant game and expect possible rebuilding. If performance worsens temporarily during shader compilation, that does not prove the cleanup damaged the hardware. Do not schedule frequent blanket cache deletion; repeated rebuilding can waste bandwidth and time while providing little durable capacity.

sections.heading: Avoid manual deletion of protected app folders
paragraphs: WindowsApps, WpSystem and related package locations are controlled by Windows and Microsoft Store services. Taking ownership or granting broad permissions can break updates, weaken isolation and leave the platform unable to manage installed games. Use Xbox app and Windows storage controls for those packages. A permission prompt is not an instruction to force access.

Similarly, do not remove recovery partitions, page files, hibernation files or reserved storage through an unverified gaming guide. Those features serve system purposes and require separate evaluation. If the system drive remains critically full after supported cleanup, move personal files safely or obtain qualified help rather than deleting unfamiliar root-level objects.

sections.heading: Review duplicate installers and capture files
paragraphs: Search ordinary personal folders for ISO images, launcher installers, driver packages, exported mod archives and duplicated recordings. Sort by size in File Explorer, then open or identify each item. An installer already superseded by an official current download may be replaceable, but a purchased offline installer or custom build may not be. Keep license information and checksums where appropriate.

Video captures often dominate gaming storage. Move completed clips to an external drive and play them from the destination before deleting originals. Consider trimming unneeded raw footage with a trusted editor, but keep source material required for a project. Do not delete evidence from a bug report or tournament dispute until the issue is resolved.

sections.heading: Check restore points and previous installations with context
paragraphs: Windows may offer previous installation files after an upgrade. Microsoft warns that removing Windows.old removes the option to return to the previous version through that folder. Delete it only when the current system is stable and rollback is no longer needed. Use the official Temporary files or Disk Cleanup interface, not manual folder removal.

System Restore usage and shadow storage can also consume capacity, but reducing protection has recovery consequences. Do not disable restore as a routine gaming-space tip. If restore storage appears excessive, review Microsoft's system protection guidance and preserve at least the recovery capability appropriate to the machine. Game storage convenience should not silently remove the safety net for Windows changes.

sections.heading: Verify every retained game after cleanup
paragraphs: Restart Windows, open each affected launcher and allow its library to refresh. Launch the moved or retained games, load a known save, confirm controller or mod profiles and exit normally. Check synchronization completion. If a title requests a fresh configuration, stop before overwriting and compare the backed-up folders. One verification cycle catches missing paths while the cleanup record is still fresh.

Recheck drive free space and compare it with the baseline. Document what produced the gain: one uninstall, moved captures, temporary files or another category. This prevents future cleanup from targeting the wrong folder. Keep backups through at least one successful restart and cloud synchronization on the intended account.

sections.heading: Plan sustainable capacity instead of emergency deletion
paragraphs: Leave working headroom for Windows updates, game patches and temporary extraction. There is no universal free-space percentage for every drive and launcher, so use the requirements of your actual titles and monitor trends. Set capture limits, archive completed projects and uninstall finished games before the drive reaches a critical state. A monthly review is safer than a frantic purge during a release-day update.

Maintain a simple inventory of important saves, their backup date and the account used. Test external storage health and replace a drive that reports errors rather than treating cleanup as repair. If game libraries routinely exceed capacity, consider a compatible larger drive only after checking the PC, interface, warranty and budget. Buying storage is optional; disciplined library management can often postpone it without risking progress.

items.title: Gaming Laptop Thermal Throttling: How to Diagnose Slowdowns Safely
items.dek: A repeatable method to distinguish normal boost behavior from heat-related clock reductions, power limits, blocked airflow, background load and hardware faults.
items.author: GAMIC News Editorial Desk
items.imageAlt: Original editorial diagram of a gaming laptop, temperature graph, fan and controlled test timeline
items.imageCredit: Original topic-specific vector illustration created in-house by GAMIC News
items.imageRights: Copyright GAMIC News; original editorial artwork with no third-party logos or game assets
body: Thermal throttling is a protective reduction in processor or graphics performance when temperature, electrical or platform limits are reached. To diagnose it, reproduce one short game sequence while recording frame time, CPU and GPU temperature, clock speed, power and utilization. Compare the start of the run with the point where performance falls. A hot laptop is not proof of throttling, and one temperature number is not enough.

The useful question is whether a limit activates at the same moment that sustained clocks and frame performance drop. Begin with the original charger, a hard flat surface, default performance settings and no overclock. Change one factor at a time. Stop if the machine smells hot, powers off, has a swollen battery, a damaged connector or a fan that does not spin.

This guide avoids universal temperature promises because processors and laptop designs have different control targets. Manufacturer documentation and diagnostic tools remain the primary references for a specific model. The goal is a safe, versioned comparison that can be handed to the laptop maker, not a risky attempt to force maximum clocks at any cost.
takeaways: Measure clock, temperature, power, utilization and frame time together during one repeatable workload.
Test on a hard surface with the correct charger and default settings before changing firmware or voltages.
Separate CPU, GPU, power and game bottlenecks; a high temperature alone does not prove throttling.
Stop and seek qualified service for shutdowns, battery swelling, damaged power connectors or failed fans.

sections.heading: What thermal throttling actually means
paragraphs: Modern laptop processors constantly adjust clock speed and voltage. Short boosts above a listed base clock are normal, as are later reductions when a workload becomes sustained. Thermal throttling is one reason for a reduction, but current, power, firmware and workload limits can produce a similar graph. A thin gaming laptop may also share a cooling or power budget between the CPU and GPU, so one component can slow when the other becomes busier without either being defective.

Do not diagnose from the case temperature or a single maximum reading. The keyboard deck can feel hot while internal control remains within the manufacturer's design, and a sensor can briefly touch a limit without a visible performance loss. The stronger pattern is synchronized evidence: temperature or a reported limit rises, effective clock and power fall, and frame time worsens during the same repeatable scene. Record the pattern instead of chasing an internet temperature threshold for a different machine.

sections.heading: Create a safe baseline before testing
paragraphs: Use the charger supplied for the laptop or an officially supported replacement with the required power rating. Connect it directly, place the computer on a rigid desk, and make sure the intake and exhaust openings are not covered. Soft bedding can block an underside intake. Let the machine reach an ordinary idle state, pause downloads, close unnecessary launchers and record the Windows power mode and the laptop utility profile. Restore CPU, GPU and memory tuning to defaults.

Restart once and use the same display, resolution, refresh rate and game settings for every comparison. Disconnecting every peripheral or disabling security software creates too many differences; remove only an optional device that is directly suspected. Note ambient conditions approximately because a hot room changes cooling headroom. Do not open a warranty-covered laptop merely to begin diagnosis, and do not use compressed air in a way that overspeeds or damages a fan.

sections.heading: Choose one repeatable game sequence
paragraphs: Select a built-in benchmark or a two-to-five-minute route through the same save. A benchmark is helpful only if it represents the slowdown you experience. Keep the frame cap, upscaler, graphics API and ray-tracing settings unchanged. Run the sequence from a fresh start, then repeat it after the system is warm. Record average performance if available, but prioritize frame-time behavior because a short severe hitch can disappear inside an average frame-rate number.

If the first run is slower only while shaders compile, the thermal hypothesis weakens. If performance begins high and then settles to a stable lower level, that can be normal boost exhaustion rather than a fault. A repeating saw-tooth pattern—clocks and frame rate fall, temperature drops, then both recover—can be more suggestive of a limit cycle. Preserve screenshots or a short log with timestamps so each change can be compared against the same phase of the workload.

sections.heading: Monitor the smallest useful set of signals
paragraphs: Use the laptop maker's diagnostic utility or one reputable monitoring tool. Record CPU and GPU utilization, effective clock, temperature and power, plus frame time. Fan speed is useful when the model exposes it. Avoid running several hardware monitors together because they can poll the same sensors, add overlays and complicate the test. A logging interval fast enough to show the transition is preferable to a screen full of unrelated voltage rails.

Interpret the signals as a system. Near-full GPU utilization with stable clocks usually points to a graphics-limited workload rather than CPU thermal throttling. Low GPU utilization alongside one saturated CPU thread can indicate a CPU or game-engine limit. Both utilizations may fall when the game waits on storage, networking or shader work. A reported thermal or power-limit flag is helpful, but match it to the exact time of the slowdown before calling it causal.

sections.heading: Separate CPU, GPU and platform limits
paragraphs: Reduce only the graphics resolution for one comparison. If frame rate rises substantially and the GPU remains highly utilized, the original run was likely GPU constrained. If resolution barely changes performance while one or more CPU threads are busy, CPU or engine work becomes more plausible. This is a diagnostic test, not a permanent optimization. Restore the original setting afterward so the next comparison remains controlled.

Laptop firmware may redistribute power between processors. A scene with heavy CPU simulation can leave less budget for the GPU, while a graphics-heavy scene can do the reverse. Some utilities label this behavior with vendor-specific terms. Consult the model manual rather than assuming that a lower clock equals overheating. If the slowdown appears only on battery, examine the power policy and supported charger behavior first; demanding games commonly reduce performance away from mains power by design.

sections.heading: Check fans and airflow without unsafe disassembly
paragraphs: Listen for a fan that never starts, grinds or changes abruptly. Inspect external vents under good light and remove loose surface dust according to the manufacturer's care instructions. Do not insert tools through the grille. Raising the rear slightly with a stable non-slip stand can be a controlled airflow test if it does not obstruct vents. If that change consistently delays the slowdown, airflow deserves attention, but it does not identify whether internal dust, a fan, thermal interface or chassis design is responsible.

An external cooling pad can be tested after the baseline, but it should not be used to conceal a failed internal fan. Record its model and fan setting. Large claimed temperature improvements from an unrelated laptop are not evidence for yours because vent layout matters. If the model's service manual permits cleaning and you have the skill, follow it exactly; otherwise use an authorized or qualified service provider, especially when battery removal or fragile ribbon cables are involved.

sections.heading: Verify the power path
paragraphs: Check that Windows recognizes normal mains power and that the battery does not repeatedly switch between charging and discharging during the test. A loose connector, under-rated USB-C supply or dock can limit available power even though the charging icon appears. Use the laptop's designated gaming power input when the manual requires it. Inspect the cable and plug for heat damage, bending or intermittent contact, and stop using damaged equipment.

Do not defeat charger identification or buy an unverified high-wattage adapter. If performance is normal with the original direct-connected supply but degrades through a dock, the dock, cable or negotiated power may be the constraint. A battery that is swollen, unusually hot or lifting the case is a safety issue, not a benchmark problem. Shut the system down, disconnect power if safe and follow the manufacturer's battery-service guidance.

sections.heading: Rule out software and background-load lookalikes
paragraphs: Use Task Manager to check whether an update, antivirus scan, browser process, capture encoder or cloud sync becomes active when performance falls. Preserve normal security protections; the goal is to identify load, not disable safety. A game overlay or recording tool can affect frame pacing, so test one optional overlay at a time. A driver update can also invalidate shader caches, causing first-run work that improves on the second comparable run.

Verify the game files if the problem affects only one title and persists after the controlled baseline. Check official game and GPU-driver known issues before reinstalling Windows or clearing every cache. A background CPU task should be visible in utilization and process history, while a storage wait may appear as disk activity with low processor use. These patterns keep a software delay from being mislabeled as heat simply because the fans are audible.

sections.heading: Use power modes as a diagnostic, not a cure
paragraphs: Microsoft documents Windows power modes, and many gaming laptops add quiet, balanced and performance profiles. Record the current mode, then compare one lower supported mode using the same route. If the lower mode produces slightly less peak performance but stable frame times and much lower temperature, the system may be operating near its sustained cooling envelope. That result does not by itself prove a defect or justify unsupported tuning.

Avoid random registry power plans, hidden firmware menus and copied undervolt values. Firmware updates can change allowed voltage control, and an unstable undervolt can create crashes that resemble the original problem. If the manufacturer offers an official profile reset or diagnostic, use that route. The safest long-term configuration is a supported mode that meets your workload without cycling, excessive noise or shutdowns—not necessarily the highest short benchmark score.

sections.heading: When firmware or drivers are relevant
paragraphs: Check the laptop maker's support page for the exact model and operating system. Read release notes before installing BIOS, embedded-controller, chipset or graphics updates. A firmware update carries more risk than changing a game setting and should not be used as an exploratory first step. Maintain stable power, follow the official procedure and never interrupt the process. Record the previous and new versions so the result is attributable.

If throttling began immediately after a graphics-driver update, use a controlled driver comparison rather than changing cooling hardware. If it began after firmware, contact the manufacturer and check whether rollback is supported; do not force an unofficial downgrade. Driver and firmware changes can alter fan curves and power sharing, but hardware symptoms such as a dead fan or damaged connector still require physical service.

sections.heading: Know when to stop and request service
paragraphs: Stop testing if the laptop shuts down, emits a burning smell, shows battery swelling, has liquid damage, produces artifacts before the operating system loads, or reports a fan error. Repeatedly forcing a thermal shutdown is not a meaningful stress test. Back up important data while the machine is stable, then contact the manufacturer or a qualified technician. Describe the exact workload and attach the concise logs rather than stating only that it becomes hot.

Service evidence should include the model and serial where appropriate, BIOS version, Windows and driver versions, power supply used, room conditions, game build, settings, time until slowdown, and the synchronized temperature, clock, power and frame-time change. State which supported profiles and external airflow checks were tried. A reproducible five-minute record is more actionable than hours of uncontrolled benchmarks.

sections.heading: A practical decision sequence
paragraphs: Begin with the correct charger, hard surface, open vents and default settings. Reproduce one route and log the minimal signals. If performance remains stable, compare the real scenario that originally failed. If it drops, identify whether GPU, CPU, power, background load or storage changes at the same time. Test one lower supported power profile, one resolution change and one airflow change only when each answers a specific question.

If the evidence points to a software regression, verify the game and use official driver guidance. If the evidence points to airflow or a fan, follow the model's service route. If behavior is stable but below expectations, compare it with the manufacturer's documented configuration, not an overclocked review sample. Keep the final working settings and the original log; the value of the diagnosis is that another person can repeat it safely.

items.author: Rédaction GAMIC News
items.title: Game Uses the Integrated GPU on a Laptop: Verify It Before Forcing a Fix
items.dek: A Windows checklist for identifying which GPU actually renders a game, setting a per-app preference, and separating hybrid-display routing from a real performance fault.
items.imageAlt: Original GAMIC News diagram of a laptop routing a game between integrated and discrete GPUs through a hybrid display path
items.imageCredit: Original illustration created in-house by GAMIC News
items.imageRights: Copyright GAMIC News; no third-party artwork, logos or game assets used
body: A laptop can show activity on its integrated GPU even while the discrete GPU renders a game. Hybrid designs may pass the finished frame through the integrated graphics processor that owns the internal display. Therefore an integrated-GPU graph, a display name or a cable attached to the laptop does not by itself prove that the game selected the wrong renderer.

Microsoft exposes per-application graphics preferences when a Windows device has more than one GPU. AMD and NVIDIA also document switchable or hybrid graphics behavior. These systems balance performance and battery life, but the exact routing depends on the laptop design, drivers, power mode, display connection and executable that launches the game.

The safe approach is to identify the rendering engine, establish a plugged-in baseline, select the correct executable in Windows, restart the title and measure again. This guide avoids disabling hardware, editing firmware or deleting drivers until the evidence shows an actual fault.
takeaways: Integrated-GPU activity can be normal on a hybrid laptop and is not proof of wrong rendering.
Apply the Windows graphics preference to the executable that renders the game, not merely the launcher.
Use the laptop maker’s documented drivers and modes before forcing firmware or device changes.

sections.heading: Understand render GPU versus display GPU
paragraphs: On a hybrid notebook, the discrete GPU can render frames and transfer them to the integrated GPU for presentation on the internal panel. NVIDIA’s Optimus description explicitly documents this type of path. Task Manager may therefore show copy or display-engine activity on the integrated adapter while the discrete adapter’s 3D engine does the heavy work. Inspect the engine labels, not only the overall percentage.

Some laptops include a multiplexer or Advanced Optimus path that can connect the internal panel differently, while an external port may be wired to one GPU. These designs vary by model. Consult the laptop manual or manufacturer utility before assuming an HDMI or USB-C port bypasses the integrated GPU. The goal is to identify the real topology, not to force every machine into the same diagram.

sections.heading: Capture a plugged-in performance baseline
paragraphs: Connect the manufacturer-supplied power adapter, select the documented performance mode, close unrelated heavy tasks and launch a repeatable scene. Record frame rate, frame time, CPU use, temperatures, clock rates and each GPU engine. Battery operation may intentionally limit the discrete GPU or total platform power, so a battery-only result is not a fair baseline for maximum gaming performance.

Note the game build, resolution, preset and whether an external display is connected. Do not change five settings at once. If performance is already consistent with the hardware’s supported range and the discrete GPU shows 3D activity, integrated activity is probably normal routing. If the discrete GPU remains idle while the integrated 3D engine is saturated, continue the selection checks.

sections.heading: Find the executable that performs the rendering
paragraphs: Many games start through a launcher, updater, anti-cheat bootstrapper or store client and then spawn another executable. Windows graphics preference must target the process that performs the rendering. Use Task Manager details while the game is running to identify the executable and its installed path. Avoid choosing an untrusted file with a similar name from a download or temporary folder.

Store applications may appear through a packaged-app selector rather than a normal Browse dialog. Follow the current Windows interface for the application type. If a game updates into a new directory or executable name, verify the preference again. Applying high performance to the launcher alone can leave the actual game under the default policy.

sections.heading: Set the per-app preference in Windows
paragraphs: In Windows 11, open System, Display, Graphics, choose the game and select Options. Microsoft documents power-saving and high-performance choices when multiple GPUs are present. Select high performance for the verified game executable, save and fully restart the title. The change does not reliably migrate into a process that was already running.

Record which adapter Windows names for each option. Do not assume “high performance” maps to the expected device without reading the label. Test the same scene after restart and compare GPU engines and frame time. If nothing changes, confirm that the correct executable was selected before changing drivers or disabling adapters.

sections.heading: Check the laptop maker’s control mode
paragraphs: Manufacturer utilities may expose hybrid, discrete-only, eco or automatic modes. These controls can require a reboot and may be unavailable on battery. Read the model-specific documentation because names are not standardized. Save the original mode and use the vendor’s supported sequence. A discrete-only mode can increase power use and heat, so it is not automatically the best everyday setting.

If the laptop has a hardware or firmware multiplexer, switching it changes display routing rather than merely an app preference. Compare hybrid and discrete modes only after the Windows per-app test, and keep other settings fixed. Do not flash unofficial firmware or modify hidden BIOS options to imitate another model. Unsupported routing changes can disable the internal display or recovery path.

sections.heading: Keep integrated and discrete drivers compatible
paragraphs: Hybrid graphics depends on both adapters. AMD’s switchable-graphics guidance notes that missing drivers can prevent the feature from working and recommends compatible integrated and discrete packages. Start with the laptop manufacturer’s supported bundle when the model uses customized power, display or multiplexer behavior. Record versions before updating.

Do not disable the integrated GPU in Device Manager as a first fix. On systems where it drives the internal display, that can remove brightness control, video acceleration, external ports or even the visible desktop. If a vendor support procedure requires driver removal, preserve recovery options and follow the documented order rather than using a generic cleanup ritual.

sections.heading: Test power, temperature and platform limits
paragraphs: A discrete GPU can be selected correctly and still run slowly because the power adapter is not recognized, the battery is low, the laptop is in quiet mode, or temperature limits reduce clocks. Check the charging indicator, adapter wattage and manufacturer diagnostics. Compare observed GPU power and clock behavior with the model’s supported documentation, not a desktop card with the same marketing name.

Let the system cool, clear external vent obstructions and repeat the scene. If performance starts high and falls as temperature rises, selection is not the main problem. Do not use unsafe fan, voltage or firmware tools to mask it. A cooling or power fault needs a different report than a game that consistently renders on the wrong adapter from launch.

sections.heading: Use an external display as a diagnostic, not a myth
